High spot amplitudes up to 19259 ppm in rotation sectors suggest wide sector-sector depth systematics need ground detrending and RV mass test
dossier.public_summary: The 14.2-day dip is faint (SNR 10, 3.4 Earth radii implied) but its depth changes by more than a factor of seven between sectors and individual transits do not match, so it is not a steady planetary transit. With no secure centroid and a large out-of-transit signal near the eclipse period, the pattern matches a diluted or blended eclipsing binary rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes 142.2% between sectors, with depth in sector 24 undetected at 1956+/-2200 ppm vs 15285+/-1656 ppm in sector 78, and changes_within_a_source true (p_constant 3.183625718859217e-06).

Individual transit depths vary strongly: chi2 29.418599131372886 dof 4, p_consistent 6.426717166228876e-06, with top 3 transits carrying 0.932 of the signal, indicating the dip comes from few/blended events.

Large out-of-transit swing on the transit period with non-zero secondary snr 2.188 near phase 0.2494 and best_brightening_snr 3.112, plus RUWE 1.036 and star_density_penalty 36.35 point to blended binary rather than planet.

No on-target centroid to confirm planet and many faint neighbours within 150 arcsec could cause the dip with deeper eclipses; combined with inconsistent depths the best explanation is a blended binary/variability, not a quiet planet.
